newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former Mitterrand aide sues for slander over book.
newsitem.headline: Former Mitterrand aide sues for slander over book.

text.p: A former aide to late French President Francois Mitterrand demanded five million francs ($850,000) damages on Monday from a member of Mitterrand's anti-terrorism unit who alleged the aide ordered the murder of a top official.

Gilles Menage, former head of Mitterrand's private office, sued ex-police captain Paul Barril and publisher Albin Michel at a Paris court for slander following publication of the book "Secret Wars at the Elysee".

The book alleges that Menage and fellow Mitterrand confidant Michel Charasse ordered the killing in 1994 of Francois de Grossouvre, a long-time Mitterrand friend and adviser on espionage who fell out of favour with the president.
Grossouvre was found dead with a bullet wound to the head in his Elysee office in what was officially described as a suicide.
Both Menage and Charasse have rejected the allegations by Barril that they were connected to the death.
Barril wrote that Grossouvre was most probably murdered because he knew too much about corruption and other scandals undermining the Mitterrand administration.

In September a Paris court rejected an appeal made by Charasse for the book to be banned. But it ordered the publishing house to put up a sign wherever the book is on sale indicating that statements concerning Charasse are contested by him.
